interaction.model_cot: Subagent had it building clean but hadn't run tests when the session limit hit. Running the test suite surfaced a real bug in NameArena.resolve() across slab boundaries — subtract-with-overflow panic. Root-caused it via targeted eprintln instrumentation rather than guessing: slab_starts' trailing entry was doing double duty as both a fixed slab-boundary marker (needed by resolve()) and a live counter tracking building's current end (mutated on every intern() call). Those are incompatible uses of the same memory: a NameSpan minted early captures an offset relative to whatever slab_starts said AT THAT TIME, but resolve() (called much later, after more names interned) reads whatever slab_starts says NOW — and since the trailing entry kept moving, the two could disagree. Fixed by making every slab_starts entry a fixed breakpoint, set once and never mutated after — building's current end is derived on demand (start + building.len()) instead of stored redundantly. Two rounds of instrumentation were needed: first fix (make flush_slab correct the stale sentinel before finalizing) got further but not all the way; second (full redesign to fixed-breakpoints-only) actually fixed it, confirmed against the existing 10,000-entry multi-slab-boundary test.
